claude_code.supported_min_source: the .claude-plugin/marketplace.json schema this catalog ships has been stable since 2.0.0; the previous floor was never validated
claude_code.verification_method: Real direct CLI check this run — `claude --version` on the runner reports 2.1.257, the fifth consecutive run with a live CLI available, so `validated_against` and `latest_known` stay equal. `claude plugin validate --strict .agents/skills` was re-run against this live 2.1.257 CLI and passed clean, and `claude plugin marketplace add`-style catalog resolution was re-checked via `make validate` (regenerate + validate manifests; 3 plugins in sync, no drift). The 2.1.253–2.1.256 gap does not exist as public releases, so the reviewed delta is 2.1.252 → 2.1.257 in full. It was reviewed line-by-line against the catalog surface and found to have zero marketplace-manifest impact requiring a schema or field change: the plugin symlink component-path fix (below) and the headersHelper credential-log-redaction improvement (below) are the two items with any catalog-adjacent surface at all, and both were checked directly rather than assumed. **Plugin symlink component-path rejection (2.1.257).** Claude Code now refuses, with an error, a plugin's declared command, agent, skill, hooks, or other component path that turns out to be a symlink escaping the plugin's own directory — a broadening of 2.1.251's commands-only path-traversal check to every declared component-path field. Checked directly against `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (and the generated `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` / `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json`): none of this catalog's three plugin entries (`tamirs-superpowers`, `jose-claudinho`, `headhunter`) declare a `commands`, `agents`, `skills`, or `hooks` field — each carries only `name`/`source`/`description`. Also confirmed with `find . -type l`: this repository itself contains no symlinks anywhere, including under `.agents/skills/run-plugins-catalog`. Not applicable, on both counts. **MCP connection/OAuth log credential redaction (2.1.257).** Debug/error logs for MCP connections and OAuth now redact credentials carried in a server's URL or request headers. This catalog's entries are all public `github` sources with no `headersHelper` in use today (documented since 2.1.238, OAuth-retry-on-401 fixed in 2.1.248), so nothing here changes, but it hardens the exact mechanism this guide already points to for a future private/token-gated entry. Everything else in the 2.1.257 changelog (Fable 5.1, timeFormat/timeZone settings, the auto-mode Containment Escape rule, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE, `/effort s`, the stale-sandbox-mask `/doctor` warning, the auto-mode outside-working-directory read prompt, gateway `/model` picker descriptions, and the long list of host/session/IDE bug fixes and VS Code changes) is host/CLI/editor-side with no marketplace, plugin-source, or skill-loading surface. Prior verification still holds: catalog install previously verified with `claude plugin marketplace add Tamircohen28/tamirs-marketplace` followed by `claude plugin install <name>@tamirs-marketplace`.

opencode.supported_min_source: oldest version on which `skills.paths` discovery of a catalog plugin's skills was verified with `opencode debug skill`
opencode.verification_method: opencode --version on the maintainer machine; latest from registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai. OpenCode has no marketplace, so the catalog itself cannot be installed — each plugin repo is cloned and its skills verified with `opencode debug skill`

capability_gaps.marketplace: OpenCode has no plugin marketplace and no plugin manifest, so this catalog cannot be added as an install source. Each plugin repo is installed directly — clone it and point `skills.paths` at its `skills/` directory, or symlink it into the OpenCode skills directory. Every plugin in this catalog ships its own `opencode.json` and its own OpenCode install guide.
capability_gaps.catalog_discovery: There is no OpenCode equivalent of listing plugins from a remote catalog. The plugin table in this repo's README is the discovery surface; installation is then per-repo.
